Source: https://research.jfrog.com/post/litellm-hijacked-again/
Linked artifact evidence: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/47826

Changes:
- Two existing LiteLLM bulk SELECT observations move from data/db/sql to
  data/db/query. Their operation, not SQL syntax alone, chooses the home.
  This accounts for every rule in sql/litellm.yaml. The old exact consumers
  are the 4025 test runner, updated here. The only broad SQL selector is a
  classic-ASP rule with disjoint file scope. New query-parent selectors do
  not exist, so the move introduces no objective membership indirectly.
- Detection changes are separate from relocation: named projections and
  query_raw/queryRaw now join existing star SELECT and rawquery/execute APIs.
  Six source-language clients use call/argument facts; PHP uses bound syntax
  because its member-call projection currently loses the method name.
- Python query-forwarding helpers require matching helper and parameter
  identifiers, a real query API, a SQL argument and the actual LiteLLM schema.
- The HTTP helper trait binds the request URL parameter, returned response
  text, fetched result, executor argument and compile/exec parameter. It is
  neutral deployment. The hostile composite adds a detached process and
  interpreter-mandated startup-module filename. No campaign URL, token,
  helper spelling, interval or dropped lock filename supplies conviction.
- Existing python-github-credential-file-harvest moves from credential-access/
  files/config to exfiltration/stealer/dev-secret and is renamed
  python-source-control-credential-post. Its two sources are source-control
  stores, and it requires HTTP POST. Evidence, severity, scope and proximity
  are preserved; the description now states its co-occurrence semantics.
  No exact consumers exist. Old parent selectors still see the required
  source-control-read constituent; the profiled collector's combined config/
  dev-secret selector retains the relocated member and matching evidence.
- Plain quoted-source origin is a metadata fact shared by the new exclusions
  and the original compiled-executor rule. Its predicate and effective Python
  scope are unchanged for the existing consumer. Explicit positive and
  synthetic-layer near misses verify that suppression.

Nearest competing placements: SQL syntax alone is data/db/sql, but these
rules require query calls. Unsynced SQL text passed to a logger is excluded.
The new remote helper is a neutral source-to-evaluator link; startup durability
belongs to persistence/system/python-startup. Source-control store plus send
belongs to exfiltration/stealer/dev-secret, not credential-access.

Rebuild controls (outputs belong in cleave's fixtures):
python3 testdata/litellm-jfrog-4033/generate-controls.py \
  --sample /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-c608bc37/scratch/threat-feed/4033/testdata/suspicious/sitecustomize.py \
  --fixtures /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/tests/fixtures/litellm-jfrog-4033
python3 testdata/litellm-jfrog-4033/check.py \
  --fixtures /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/tests/fixtures/litellm-jfrog-4033 \
  --report /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-c608bc37/scratch/threat-feed/4033/controls.json

43 focused cases passed. Seven backup controls have no suspicious/hostile
findings. Explicit Windows/macOS scans verify the fork-based platform boundary.
Final atomscan: 2 hostile and 1 suspicious on the one unchanged reconstructed
sample. Original wheels were unavailable (PyPI returned 404); no payload ran.
Hashes, PURLs, scoped endpoints and fuller evidence notes are retained in the
article's scratch/threat-feed/4033 tree. No clean version/hash or inferred Go
source-package identity is included. Required final gate: make validate.

The full validator exposed dynamic-import false positives on Cruhon quoted
code-generation templates. The existing Base64/zlib import atoms now require
actual __import__ calls with their exact module argument, and exclude plain
quoted source layers. Scope is Python, where call facts are available. Four
additional controls preserve real imports and reject comments, string data and
unrelated module names. The unchanged Cruhon fixture scores 4 against cap 5.
